scores.name: Artie Ficial
scores.reason: Concrete resignation motive now combines with an admitted visit to the set place and an order keeping the poison bottle off display. The latter may be responsible caution, but joins both relevant locations.

scores.name: Claire O’Scuro
scores.reason: Moved the bottle's incoming papers and saw intake files, giving potential knowledge of contradictory descriptions. No direct cupboard or glass access is yet shown.

scores.name: Hugh Bidder
scores.reason: Arranged the Velvet Widow purchase and concealed the seller's conflicting liquid description, adding likely knowledge of the cyanide source to his business-ending motive. Glass access remains unproven.

scores.name: Monet Bags
scores.reason: Admits the hold caused the unattended interval and her invoice was at Grant's place with his glass. This puts her near the target, though the budget explanation is plausible.

scores.name: Chip Patina
scores.reason: Applied the closure band and checked the bottle, giving direct source access and knowledge of its condition. His admitted paperwork fraud supplies pressure, but no glass visit is shown.

scores.name: Dada DiCapo
scores.reason: Admits entering the room while the place was set and attempting a rejected toast cue. Opportunity and grievance increase suspicion, without poison knowledge.

scores.name: Sue Venir
scores.reason: Removed the agreement from Grant's set place without authorization. Professional exposure now combines with access to the glass area, but legal intervention explains the visit.

scores.name: Dr. Art E. Fact
scores.reason: Knew the purchase attachment required original contents despite the inert loan description and saw objects at preview. Source knowledge is stronger, but access to Grant's glass is not established.

scores.name: Tess Tament
scores.reason: Personally arranged privacy and visited the waiting glass while furious with Grant. This is substantial opportunity, but no cyanide-source access is shown.

scores.name: Barb Dwyer
scores.reason: Disabled observation, restricted outsiders, and checked the set room herself. Security position could provide source access too, though an actual cupboard visit is not stated.

scores.name: Paige Turner
scores.reason: Concealed a recording excerpt and searched Grant's coat, but neither action connects her to the poison bottle or set glass.

scores.name: Anya Tique
scores.reason: Admits spare-key access to the preparation cupboard while the bottle was there. Her denial of opening it is uncorroborated, and the removed founding memo supplies concealment pressure.

scores.name: Reed DeLabel
scores.reason: Removed an original-contents warning from the bottle press entry while retaining the full file. Could know the poison risk and help conceal it, but neither glass nor bottle handling is proven.

scores.name: Brie DeVivre
scores.reason: Admits taking a drink ingredient to Grant's set place and leaving its container there, providing a direct, plausible poison-transfer route. Her unpaid-course motive is weaker than Hugh's, but means and opportunity are stronger.

scores.name: Robin Banks
scores.reason: Saw the bottle and handled intake papers, giving general source awareness. His actions focus on the bowl and public interview, without direct toast access.

unique_reason: Several guests admit access to the set glass, while several others handled the bottle or knew its contradictory descriptions. Brie has a direct ingredient route and Hugh has particularly strong knowledge and motive, but no exclusive source-to-glass chain is established.
naturalism_notes: The individual acts produce useful overlapping opportunity instead of one obvious culprit. Nearly every guest again offers a polished confession and an exact relevance to paperwork or access, making the questioning feel mechanically complete. Original contents versus inert liquid requires careful tracking across seller, loan, catalog, and press records; a clear chronological record could reduce confusion. Anya's old spare key is plausible but conveniently broadens cupboard access.
